phase3_findings.description: Widget render test checks only 5 of 8 row-rule kinds (not any_of, owner_via, referenced_by or its link) and no rendered source values; loading/empty/error/narrow states have no behavior test.
Assertion that two configs built back to back have different loaded_at timestamps depends on clock resolution and can fail spuriously.
No test covers Config.loaded_at raising RuntimeError for a never-validated config and get_access_rules returning it as isError.
LoadedRuleSets.sha256 defaults to an empty string, not a valid SHA-256; correctness relies on the single caller load_rule_sets.
_loaded_at is set once in the after-validator; Config is not frozen, so reassigning rule_sets or rls later changes the listing without changing the load time.
typed_value raises TypeError for an unsupported type and the get_access_rules handler catches only RuntimeError; unreachable with today's strict field types.
Doc says the widget has 'a name search', but the search also matches rule-set scope and table names and filters flat RLS rules by table. Capped by the behavior-inert prose cap (all three limbs held).
The .catch after app.connect() also catches render errors and callTool rejections from load(), labelling all of them 'Failed to connect to host'; the underlying message is still shown.

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (9)

<details><summary>9 items</summary>

1. `tests/unit/test_access_rules.py` lines 359-398: `test_widget_renders_each_value_with_its_type` checks how the widget renders only 5 of the 8 row-rule kinds (`all_of`, `inherit`, `compare`, `is_null`, `is_not_null`). It does not check `any_of`, `owner_via`, `referenced_by` or a `referenced_by` node's nested `link`, and it does not check rendered source-field values. The loading, empty, error and narrow-width states have no behavior test. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `tests/unit/test_access_rules.py` line 236 asserts that two configs built one after the other have different `loaded_at` timestamps. On a platform with a coarse clock both can get the same timestamp, so the test can fail when nothing is wrong. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/config.py`: no test covers the path where `Config.loaded_at` raises `RuntimeError` for a config that was never validated and `get_access_rules` returns it as `isError`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 734-735: `LoadedRuleSets.sha256` defaults to `""`, which is not a valid SHA-256. Only the single caller, `load_rule_sets`, keeps the listed hash correct. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/config.py` lines 850-868: `_loaded_at` is set once in the after-validator. `Config` is not frozen, so reassigning `cfg.rule_sets` or `cfg.rls` later changes the listing while the load time stays the same. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `src/sqllens/access_rules.py` lines 213-229: `typed_value` raises `TypeError` for an unsupported value type, and the `get_access_rules` handler in `server.py` catches only `RuntimeError`. No value that can reach it today triggers this. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `src/sqllens/ui/access_rules.html` lines 406-411: the `.catch` after `app.connect()` also catches render errors and `callTool` rejections that happen inside `load()`, and labels every one "Failed to connect to host". The underlying message is still shown. (raised by 1/6 agents)
8. `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` line 525 says the widget has "a name search". The search also matches a rule set's `scope` and its table names, and it filters flat RLS rules by table. acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With `[access_rules] allow_admin_tools` unset or `false`, the server lists neither the `get_access_rules` tool nor the `ui://sqllens/access-rules.html` resource. With it `true`, it lists both, and the tool takes no arguments.
- [ ] `tools/list` shows `get_access_rules` with `_meta.ui.visibility` equal to `["app"]`. The server itself does not act on that field: it lists the tool to every client and runs a `tools/call` for it from any client.
- [ ] While the switch is on, `get_access_rules` answers every caller that passes the server's authentication, with no check of who the caller is.
- [ ] `get_access_rules` reports only the process it runs in. When the switch is on only in a separate admin instance, the result shows that instance's load time and catalog-check state, not those of the instance that serves end users.
- [ ] For a configuration with flat `[[rls]]` rules, `get_access_rules` returns each rule's table, column, operator, and static value or `value_from_metadata` key. The flat-RLS part of the result carries no hash.
- [ ] The widget shows every value in the result exactly as the server loaded it, with its type: a string, an integer, a float or a boolean. This covers flat-RLS values and their list members and the values in rule-set fields and row rules. An integer keeps every digit (for example `9007199254740993`, which a plain JavaScript `JSON.parse` would show as `9007199254740992`). A float keeps its float type even when its value is whole (`1.0` shows as a float, not as the integer `1`). A non-finite float shows as `nan`, `inf` or `-inf`. A rule with `value = inf` and one with `value = "inf"` show different types. The tool's whole result parses with a strict JSON parser that rejects `NaN` and `Infinity`.
- [ ] For a configuration with a rule-set file, `get_access_rules` returns the file path, the `binding` database and account IDs, and the `metadata` key names. For each set it returns its name, its `scope`, and every `source` field the file sets. It returns each table's `columns`, `predicate_columns` and `row_rule`.
- [ ] A returned `row_rule` is a nested tree that keeps every node the file defines. A fixture covering all eight kinds on `main` (compare, is_null, is_not_null, any_of, all_of, owner_via, inherit and referenced_by) shows each node. The fixture also covers an `inherit` node with a `parent_rule` and a `referenced_by` node with a `link`, and both show their nested parts.
- [ ] The returned rule-set hash equals the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file's bytes as `load_rule_sets` read them. For a file with CRLF line endings, it equals `sha256sum` of that file. Changing or deleting the file after the server loaded it does not change the hash or the rules `get_access_rules` returns.
- [ ] A rule-set file that loads today loads to the same rules after the change, including a file with CRLF or bare-CR line endings. A file that fails to load today fails with the same error message.
- [ ] `get_access_rules` returns, for each rule set, whether requests that select it are refused because `confirmed_against_production` is not `true`. It also returns the process's current catalog-check state: `false` before the check has passed and `true` after it has.
- [ ] `get_access_rules` returns the time the configuration holding the returned rules was loaded, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. Two calls in one process return the same time.
- [ ] With neither flat RLS rules nor a rule-set file configured, `get_access_rules` returns a successful result that says no access rules are loaded. When `rule_sets.file` is set but the file was never loaded, it returns `isError: true` with a message saying so.
- [ ] The widget calls only `get_access_rules`, and only through the host (`callServerTool`). It makes no direct network request. It has no control that edits, adds or deletes a rule.
- [ ] The widget resource is served with `app-with-deps.js` inlined, so its HTML contains no `./vendor/` import.

checklist.verify_against: src/sqllens/runtime.py and profiles.py config copies; pydantic PrivateAttr copy semantics
checklist.verify_hint: Check how runtime.py/profiles.py derive effective configs and whether build_server's cfg is the validated instance
checklist.evidence: Repo side verified: config.py:850-861 declares _loaded_at as a PrivateAttr and the after-validator _load_rule_sets sets it on each validated construction (Config.load -> cls() at config.py:931; env-only and TOML go through the same path). runtime.py and profiles.py contain no Config copies (no model_copy/copy; they build effective settings, not Config objects). The only Config model_copy in src is eval/runner.py:87 (verification_config), which copies a validated cfg with update=; model_copy does not re-run validators, so _loaded_at would only be retained if pydantic's __copy__ copies __pydantic_private__. That is a library behavior. No dependency_sources were supplied and pydantic is not vendored in the views, so I could not read pydantic's BaseModel.model_copy/__copy__ source to confirm it. Also, access_rules.py:149 reads cfg.loaded_at and raises RuntimeError at config.py:867 for a never-validated config. Missing evidence: pydantic BaseModel.__copy__ source (pydantic/main.py).
